title: "Bass line: Roots on 1 and 3"

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Roots on 1 and 3**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

It belongs in *Folk carol*, *Hymn (four parts)*, *Piano ballad* and *Acoustic strum*. Here it is in the folk carol style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-held.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Roots on 1 and 3, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two notes a bar, both the root. Count 1-2-3-4 aloud and pluck on 1 and 3. Let each note last its full two beats; the gap before the next one should be tiny. When a bar has two chords, the second root simply arrives on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}},{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G C|D G|C D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>
